about:
Franklin Braid Manufacturing operates from Emporia, Virginia, where it has been based since 1956. The business traces its roots to 1944, when Wick Narrow Fabric Company purchased a plant in Franklin, Virginia, to produce flat braided tapes. In 1980 the company became a subsidiary of Wayne Mills, a family-owned textile mill founded in 1910 in Philadelphia, and the two remain sister operations today.

The company produces braided, woven, and knitted cords, ropes, and elastic products — including drawstring elastic, furniture elastic, and medical-grade elastic — on more than 2,000 machines, among them high-speed European braiders. Its 80,000-square-foot facility employs 90 people and runs at a rate exceeding 20 million feet of product per week. A dedicated finishing line handles custom coatings and special finishes to customer specifications.

Franklin Braid serves a global customer base across apparel, bags, home furnishings, medical, outdoor, agriculture, fishing, military, filtration, awning, and other industrial markets. Customers range from military-grade specifiers to consumer-goods brands seeking bulk volumes of polyester, cotton, nylon, and other yarn-based products.

The company emphasizes its ability to create specialty products for unique applications, working with virtually any yarn type and developing custom constructions to supplied specifications. That flexibility, combined with in-house finishing and high-volume capacity, is presented as its core differentiator.
